Calls from the US-established Board of Peace, the UN and the EU have gone unanswered.

author: Al Jazeera English
description:
Two decades of AJE: Shaping media, amplifying unheard voices and driving global conversations.

In November 2006, Al Jazeera English went live with an audacious mandate: to challenge the traditional hegemony of Western media conglomerates and structurally invert the global news flow by providing a localised, uncompromising perspective from the Global South to the English-speaking world. To mark its 20th anniversary, this documentary delivers a definitive, multilayered chronicle of AJE's trajectory from a disruptive alternative to dominant Western news media to the globally consumed news source it is today. The film seamlessly pairs an outside-in investigative lens with ground-up human testimony and internal insights. The film reflects on AJE’s historic coverage of global conflicts, the climate crisis, genocide and more in a drastically changing media landscape, all while balancing difficult decisions regarding where to focus resources, battling stigma as state-funded media and weather
title: Twenty Years of Al Jazeera English: The Counternarrative | Featured Documentary

Southeast Asian leaders are gathering in the Philippines for the ASEAN Summit. Talks are expected to focus on trade, regional security and an energy crisis linked to the war on Iran. US President Donald Trump is expected on Tuesday, while disputes over the South China Sea and the conflict in Myanmar are also on the agenda.

Al Jazeera’s Barnaby Lo says most meetings hosted by the Philippines as chair have focused on the economic impact of the war on Iran and the closure of the Strait of Hormuz. The Philippines imports 99 percent of its fuel and was the first country to declare a state of energy emergency. The Philippines, Indonesia and Thailand have signed an agreement giving the Philippines priority access to Thai and Indonesian fuel stockpiles if it runs out.

Talks will also cover a South China Sea code of conduct under negotiation for more than 20 years. Philippine Foreign Secretary Maria Teresa Lazaro says 80 percent has been finalised.

The presidents of the United States, China and Russia are set to hold trilateral talks next week.

Donald Trump, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin are due to meet on Thursday in the Chinese city of Shenzhen, on the sidelines of the APEC summit. The meeting could bring the leaders of three of the world’s biggest nuclear powers to the same table. They are expected to discuss the war with Iran and a possible agreement on nuclear arms.

Al Jazeera’s Matthew Torres says it will be the first time all three leaders are in one room for trilateral talks. The White House and the Kremlin have confirmed the meeting.

Torres says the US wants to start talks on a broader nuclear arms agreement, after a 2010 treaty capping warheads expired in February. Putin has suggested extending it, but Trump wants a deal that includes China. It is unclear whether Xi wants to join.

author: Al Jazeera English
description:
People across Portugal are protesting, angry at soaring rents and the rising cost of living. Demonstrations are taking place in more than 30 cities.

Protesters want more affordable housing, stronger tenant protections, and the government to scrap proposed changes to rental laws. 

Al Jazeera’s Rosie Birchard says thousands of people are on the streets of Lisbon and in cities around the country. Portugal is often described as having one of Europe’s worst housing crises. Rents and house prices have shot up in recent years, and the country has seen the biggest increase in the gap between incomes and house prices in the European Union.

With government budget talks coming up, protesters want the government to scrap proposals that could make it easier for some landlords to evict tenants. 

The government says it is open to compromise and to speaking with protesters, but they are not convinced.

Al Jazeera’s Rosie Birchard reports from Lisbon.

title: Thousands protest across Portugal over soaring rents and cost of living

description:
A car bomb has killed at least two people in Jaramana, on the southeastern edge of Damascus.

The explosion on Saturday killed a man and a girl and wounded another person. Syria’s internal security forces say they have sealed off the area and opened an investigation.

Al Jazeera’s Heidi Pett says security sources and emergency workers at the scene confirmed an explosive device was placed inside a Kia Rio. 

Pett says that while the security situation continues to improve, there have been a number of other IED and car bomb attacks in Syria over the past year, which authorities have attributed to cells or individuals linked to ISIL. 

She says the blast will have shaken people’s sense of safety, although most recent attacks have targeted security services rather than civilians.

Al Jazeera’s Heidi Pett reports from Damascus.
